no_self_promotion (AUTH-030): fits 'users can't grant themselves access'; used, but dropped is_admin from fields since the workspace has no such field
endpoints_have_tests (CHG-001): fits 'change control' only weakly (testing before a change ships, not an approval trail); used as-is
audit_log_protected (RET-001): fits 'evidence of who changed data'; used with the workspace's audit_log table and record_audit_event function
own_records_only (AUTH-020): partial fit to access; not used, the ask is about reviews and change control, not per-user data isolation, and it needs field choices I did not want to guess
one_auth_table (AUTH-050): access-related but not asked for; not used
no_destructive_sql, functions_snake_case, tables_have_listed_fields, others: no fit to change control or access review

access: users cannot change their own role from request input
change control: each endpoint has a test before it ships
change control: those tests assert something
change record: the audit log table exists
change record: only the audit function writes to the audit log

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Access reviews: periodic review that each user's access is still right, with a sign-off
Evidence that a human approved each change before it went live (change approval trail)
Evidence that the policies were run and results kept for the auditor over time
Removing access when someone leaves or changes role (access removal)
Who may change a workspace's code or policies (change permissions)

ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: the ask is ambiguous, and policies only read stored definitions, so they can show shape, not that a process ran

assumptions: The customer's 'access reviews' means access to the app and admin endpoints, not a periodic review meeting
Admin endpoints are the four in api_group 'admin' (users_GET, tenants_GET, orgs/org_id/tenants_GET, tenants/tenant_id_PATCH)
check_admin_role is the role check the admin API is meant to use
Public endpoints are the three with tags = ["public"]: login, health, newsletter subscribe
audit_log is the audit trail for change; record_audit_event is the function that should write it
Criterion tags (cc6.1, cc6.2, cc6.3, cc7.2, cc8.1) are my mapping of the SOC 2 Common Criteria; the customer's auditor should confirm the mapping
The policies are advisory, not blocking, since a new policy should not block anything until the owner decides
confusions: AUTH-002 template scopes by tags ["admin"], but the admin API endpoints only share an api_group, and no object carries an admin tag; the skill's rule to scope by tag would make this rule match nothing. I used api_groups, which the skill allows, but the template's example and scope disagree with the workspace and the skill did not say which to prefer

AUTH-030 template lists is_admin and role; the skill says to write only names the workspace has, but the template fields list is a template, and I could not tell if a template field the workspace lacks is an error or just harmless
CHG-001 is named 'Endpoints are tested', but the customer's ask is change control. The skill does not say how to decide when a template title only partly fits a compliance ask

Whether to put a SOC 2 criterion in tags is not explained: the skill says to record the criterion as a tag, but tags also decide which policies apply to objects in some checks, and the criterion tags are on policies only

The skill says a rule warning means it is wrong, but xano policy parse printed no warnings, so I could not confirm the workspace-name warnings it describes; I did not run evaluate, which the brief forbids, so I cannot tell which objects match
wished_for: A template or check for periodic access review (with a recorded sign-off), or at least a clear statement that none exists
A check that a change to an endpoint was approved (or a link to a change-approval object), for the change-control part of SOC 2
A worked example of mapping a compliance framework (e.g. SOC 2 CC6/CC8) to templates, with the criterion tags
A note on whether a template's example names (is_admin, require_admin) must be replaced with workspace names, and how to tell when a template scope matches nothing before evaluating
why_confidence: The five policies parse (exit 0, no warnings) and cover access to endpoints, admin role checks, self-promotion, endpoint tests and the audit log. But the ask is for SOC 2 evidence of change controls and access reviews, which a policy cannot prove: policies check stored definitions when they run, not that a review or approval happened, and access reviews have no check at all. I did not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden by the brief), so I cannot say which objects pass or fail.
